blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Average is calculated by dividing the total sum of observations by the total number of observations.
To find the total sum when the average is given, multiply the average by the total count of numbers.
Adding or removing a value alters both the overall sum and total count, shifting the average value.
Weighted average accounts for varying degrees of importance or group sizes across datasets.
Average of a group of numbers is a single value that represents the central value of the group.

Formula:

Average = (Sum of observations) / (Number of observations)

blocks.content: In SBIexamination, questions on average are direct, formula-based, and often linked with age, salary, marks, population and similar topics.

blocks.content: 3. FINDING SUM WHEN AVERAGE IS GIVEN

items:
Formula:

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Example:

Average age of 10 students is 18 years.

Total age = 18 × 10 = 180 years

blocks.content: 4. AVERAGE WHEN A VALUE IS ADDED OR REMOVED

Example 1:

Average of 5 numbers is 20. A new number 30 is added.

Old sum = 20 × 5 = 100

New sum = 100 + 30 = 130

New number of observations = 6

New average = 130 / 6 ≈ 21.67



Example 2:

Average of 10 numbers is 25. One number 35 is removed.

Old sum = 25 × 10 = 250

New sum = 250 − 35 = 215

New number of observations = 9

New average = 215 / 9 ≈ 23.89

items: Average age of 5 boys is 20 years and average age of 3 girls is 18 years.
Sum of boys = 5 × 20 = 100
Sum of girls = 3 × 18 = 54
Total sum = 154

Total persons = 8



Average age = 154 / 8 = 19.25 years

• Be careful when values are added or removed.

Weighted average concepts are critical for solving questions on combined group means and mixtures.
